digest.component_or_area: Mirror Guard replication check (CLI and workflow)
propositions: Mirror Guard's primary watcher (mirror-guard.yml workflow) runs a single instantaneous replication check and fails on any SHA divergence, even transient post-submit lag, while the secondary CloudWatch alarm implements a 2x5-minute sustained-divergence evaluation window to absorb expected ~15s replication lag.

The module's design (replication_verdict docstring, commit d96628c9dca) explicitly delegates transient-lag absorption to the alarm layer's sustained-divergence window, but this window was never implemented on the workflow surface, leaving a gap between design and implementation.

An in-process evaluation window in mirror_guard.py (3 samples over ~90s by default, re-sampling on divergence until convergence or failure) satisfies the designed lag-absorption portably, without depending on CI-provider state or machinery.

Convergence within the tolerance window returns exit 0 and healthy; persistent divergence (static or moving GitHub tip) returns exit 1 and unhealthy, preserving failure detection for genuine replication stalls.

Fix landed in Gerrit change 2110 (merged as 969acad79b4b): _replication_check_with_lag_tolerance wrapper, run()/main() lag_attempts and lag_delay_seconds params, CLI flags, and updated docstrings; no behavioral weakening—today's failure set minus lag-that-converges.
